items.title: Analyserte krimbøker: – Romanen du skriver med KI, er ikke den samme som du hadde skrevet uten KI
items.excerpt: Aftenposten ran a stylometric analysis of Norwegian crime bestseller Jørn Lier Horst's novels before and after he began using AI: humming, 'during' and over a hundred times as many dashes — the language measurably shifted. Centre of Norway's biggest AI-authorship row. Off-list outlet (no on-list coverage of the Horst affair).

items.title: KI-bruk i bokbransjen: – Kan ikke nekte forfattere å bruke teknologien
items.excerpt: After accusations of extensive AI use by crime writer Jørn Lier Horst, author Hilde Østby says the Norwegian book trade can't ban authors from using the technology but must set rules — disclosure and labelling are on the table. Off-list outlet.

items.title: Risikerer vi at teknologien blir portvokter for litteraturen?
items.excerpt: Norway's writers' union Forfatterforbundet says publishers now screen incoming manuscripts with AI detectors and authors are being rejected as 'written by AI' when they say they used none — it demands clear criteria before an algorithm gatekeeps literature. (Debate piece; foro3d aggregated it 11-23.) Off-list outlet.

items.title: GlobalComix's pivot to AI is just muddying the waters
items.excerpt: Heidi MacDonald on GlobalComix's new Gemini-powered discovery feed, which pulls RSS content from opted-in comics news sites (ANN, CBR, ComicBook.com) into the app. Follow-up/analysis: the GlobalComix Gemini assistant itself was carded 11-20.

items.title: Can an Indie Author Make a Whole Cozy Mystery Series Look From an Image Model? My Cover Tests
items.excerpt: Hands-on test of making a consistent three-book cozy-mystery cover series, audiobook square and thumbnails with an image model (Nano Banana Pro API, book 1 as reference), with costs vs $400-900 commissioned covers and a disclosure/ethics section. Caution: names a specific API; check for advertorial tone.

items.title: Literary Translators Warn AI Threatens Their Livelihoods in Copyright Case
items.excerpt: The American Literary Translators Association and 11 other creative groups filed an amicus brief in Authors Guild v. OpenAI/Microsoft, warning AI translation could turn translators 'from interpreters into primarily editors of large language model outputs.' (OpenAI MDL amicus angle deprioritized; this is the translator-specific brief.)

items.title: AI Training is Copyright Infringement: What Publishers Need to Know about Thomson Reuters v ROSS Intelligence
items.excerpt: Publisher-side analysis of the Third Circuit ROSS opinion: the more an AI product is marketed as solving research tasks, the less transformative its use of STM content. Follow-up — the ROSS appeal ruling itself was carded earlier.

items.title: Guest Post — Building a Taxonomy of Bots
items.excerpt: With AI crawlers and agents hammering scholarly platforms, a guest post proposes a shared taxonomy of bots so publishers can measure and manage robotic traffic.

items.title: More than 100 publishers back University Press Charter amid AI and financial pressures
items.excerpt: A new University Press Charter committing publishers to research integrity, transparency and responsible use of AI has 108 signatories from 26 countries.

items.title: AI is giving writers the support publishing cannot
items.excerpt: Comment: Marian Stan argues AI tools now give aspiring novelists the editorial feedback that traditional publishing has long failed to provide. (Opinion.)

items.title: 'AI Slop' Papers Published Under Prominent Academics' Names
items.excerpt: High-profile researchers were listed as authors of AI-generated papers in little-known journals, raising concern Ph.D. students could be lured into submitting there too.

items.title: AI 시대 편집기자 역할은…'마지막 문장은 사람이 쓴다' 발간
items.excerpt: 한국편집기자협회가 AI 시대 편집기자의 역할과 통찰을 담은 책자 '마지막 문장은 사람이 쓴다'를 발간했다. (책 발간 소식 — AI는 책의 주제.)

items.title: 한국저작권위원회-국립중앙도서관, AI 시대 도서관 사서 대상 저작권 교육 실시
items.excerpt: 한국저작권위원회와 국립중앙도서관이 전국 도서관 사서 41명을 대상으로 '인공지능 시대, 도서관에서 알아야 할 저작권 및 활용사례' 교육을 20일 진행했다.

items.title: [윤주혜의 C] 너도나도 작가님…AI가 불붙인 '딸깍 출판'
items.excerpt: AI가 써준 200쪽 원고와 돈만 있으면 책을 낼 수 있는 '딸깍 출판' 시대 — 출판사 투고와 문학상 응모가 역대 최다로 몰리며 AI 원고 판별 부담이 커졌다는 칼럼. (11-18 AI 원고 급증 카드의 후속 칼럼이라 중복 가능.)

items.title: '죄와 벌' 속 한 문장‥AI는 '절했다', 번역가는?
items.excerpt: 도스토옙스키 작품 네 편을 번역하는 데 10년을 쓴 번역가가 '죄와 벌'의 한 문장을 두고 AI 번역과 사람 번역의 차이를 짚는다 — AI 문학 번역의 한계. Off-list outlet.

items.title: 장성 주민 15명, AI로 전자그림책 작가 데뷔
items.excerpt: 전남 장성군 주민 15명이 생성형 AI를 활용해 자신만의 이야기를 전자그림책으로 출판하며 작가로 데뷔했다. Off-list outlet (small local story).

items.title: 시험도, 논문도, 문학도 '진짜'의 위기…일상에 스며드는 불신[AI發 신뢰 실종 시대①]
items.excerpt: AI 발 신뢰 위기 기획 1편 — 시험 부정, AI 가짜 논문과 함께 문학계에서도 '진짜' 작가 여부를 의심하는 풍경을 다룬다. Off-list outlet; broad feature.

items.title: Many takers for AI books at Madurai fair, but writers wary
items.excerpt: Amid the AI-generated-books scandal at Madurai's Kalaignar Centenary Library, the city's annual book fair nearby is seeing enthusiastic buyers for books on AI, while Tamil writers remain wary. (Tamil Nadu library scam carded earlier; this is a new angle.) Off-list outlet.

items.title: Libraries, books, and the question of AI
items.excerpt: Op-ed after the Tamil Nadu library scandal: what defines a good book, and should AI-translated or AI-generated books be dismissed outright from library procurement? Off-list outlet; opinion.

items.title: 'Pervert glasses' named word of the year by Macquarie dictionary, ahead of 'nudify' and 'AI;DR'
items.excerpt: Australia's Macquarie Dictionary picked 'pervert glasses' as its 2026 word of the year, with AI-era terms 'nudify' and 'AI;DR' on the shortlist (body only partly verified; AI is a shortlist theme, not the winner). (Cambridge 'human' WOTY carded 11-21.)

items.title: The Melodrama of AI Authorship
items.excerpt: Essay arguing that the way critics conflate AI writing with features of postcolonial melodrama betrays a cultural bias in literary gatekeeping. Off-list outlet; opinion.

items.title: AI could bring books to radio, but broadcasters still need to direct the story
items.excerpt: Synthetic voices could let radio stations test serialized literary readings and narrated essays, but success depends on editorial judgement, rights clearance and listener trust. Off-list outlet.
